title: Mutual fund, SIF, or PMS/AIF?
intro: Eight product traits — file each on the right rung of the access ladder.

cards.text: Can only buy securities it expects to rise, then wait
Anyone can start with a few hundred rupees a month
Shorting via derivatives, under the same SEBI oversight as mutual funds
₹10 lakh minimum — the new middle rung
Can set its own redemption windows and concentrate in a few sectors
Asked for ₹50 lakh before they would take your call
Category III vehicles starting at ₹1 crore
The 'rich people's funds' most readers were never allowed to buy

debrief: The ladder runs on two axes at once: minimum ticket (a few hundred rupees → ₹10L → ₹50L/₹1cr) and mandate freedom (long-only → shorting, concentration, custom redemptions → full hedge-fund latitude). The SIF's pitch is precisely the middle: PMS-style tools with mutual-fund-style regulation at a fraction of the entry price. What the ladder doesn't promise — as the cover story shows — is that the freedoms actually get used.
